# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 5

**5:1** On the next day Joachim brought his offerings, saying within himself: "If the Lord God is propitious toward me, the frontlet of the priest will make it manifest." He presented his gifts and watched the priest closely as he approached the altar of the Lord, observing the frontlet. He saw no sign of sin upon it. And Joachim said, "Now I know that the Lord God is propitious toward me and has remitted all my sins."

**5:2** And he went down from the temple of the Lord justified, and he returned to his house.

**5:3** And the months were completed by Anna. In the ninth month she gave birth. She asked the midwife, "What have I brought forth?" And the midwife said, "A female child." And Anna said, "My soul is magnified this day." And she laid the child down.

**5:4** When the days were fulfilled, Anna was purified and gave suck to the child, and she called her name Mary.

---

## Translator's Note

The frontlet (*petalon*) was the golden plate worn on the high priest's forehead inscribed "Holy to the LORD" (Exod 28:36-38). It was believed to reveal whether offerings were accepted. Joachim reads it as absolution. Anna's exclamation "My soul is magnified" (5:3) is the direct source of the opening words of the Magnificat in Luke 1:46 — the author of this text likely knew Luke's Gospel or its source. The naming of Mary at verse 4 brings the birth narrative to its close.
